headline: Pasqal is leading a 50 million euro European project, now moving into execution, to build factory-ready chip parts for quantum computers that use neutral atoms.
score_reason: Funded multi-country project, but the source is the lead company's own press release and no part has been delivered yet.
importance_line: European quantum builders and sensor makers could gain home-grown lasers and chips, but the three-year plan is announced by Pasqal itself and nothing has been built yet.
source: Pasqal (press release), as carried by The Quantum Insider
summary: The Quantum Insider carries a Pasqal press release saying the French-founded neutral-atom quantum computing company is coordinating Q-PLANET, a three-year, 50 million euro project co-funded by the EU's Chips Joint Undertaking with 28 partners in 11 European countries. The group will develop chip-based lasers, atom chips and tiny vapor cells for quantum computers, sensors and atomic clocks; Pasqal calls it a move from plan to execution, and the goals are its own statements.
notes: HPCwire link (the pool url) was blocked; read the same story at The Quantum Insider. Company press release; funding amounts as stated by Pasqal.
